# Fluctuations and spectra

Source papers: `Monchaux2007`, `Monchaux2009`, `Bourgoin2002`.

| Quantity | Value | Unit | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Fluctuation PDF shape | Gaussian | - | Below and above threshold |
| Low-frequency peak | 0.14 | F | Broad peak |
| Boundary spectrum exponent, f < f_low | 0 to -0.5 | - | Changes across threshold |
| Boundary spectrum exponent, f_low < f < F | -2 to -2.5 | - | Changes across threshold |
| High-frequency boundary cutoff | 1.4 | F | Exponential decay |
| Bulk axial spectrum exponent | -5/3 | - | F/10 < f < 4F |
| Bulk azimuthal/radial spectrum exponent | -1 | - | F/10 < f < 4F |
| Bulk high-frequency exponent | -11/3 | - | 4F < f < 8F |
| Burst correlation time | 2.5 | s | Autocorrelation decay |
| Burst spectrum exponent | -2 | - | Lorentzian-like |
| Reversal decay rate | 0.8 | s^-1 | Start of reversal |

quantities.notes: Fluctuation PDFs are roughly Gaussian below and above threshold.
Sharp nonlinear increase near onset; can be used as a practical threshold indicator.
Changes from about 0 below threshold to about -0.5 above threshold for f < f_low.
Changes from about -2 below threshold to about -2.5 above threshold for f_low < f < F.
High-frequency spectra are better described by exp(-f/f_exp).
For F/10 < f < 4F, axial component ~ f^-5/3.
For F/10 < f < 4F, azimuthal and radial components ~ f^-1.
Characteristic decay time of magnetic-field autocorrelation in burst regimes.
Exponential decay rate of field amplitude at the start of a reversal.
